summary: Candidate findings for extending terminology coverage: LOINC offers a versioned clinical observation vocabulary and release download mechanism, and CMS publishes a provider taxonomy crosswalk. These are broad national resources, not evidence of local hospital coding practice. This research did not acquire datasets or verify a public CCN–NPI crosswalk suitable for assigning hospital identifiers.

sources.title: Download LOINC
sources.geography: United States and international; terminology resource, not geographically specific
sources.grain: LOINC code × release, with accompanying terminology table and accessory files
observed_facts: The official download page identifies release 2.83 and names Loinc_2.83.zip; the complete package requires a LOINC account.
The official API documentation describes GET /Loinc for release metadata and GET /Loinc/Download for the archive; authentication is required.
The license permits copying and distribution with conditions including retaining the version and license notice; certain third-party content carries separate terms.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For a bounded lab-code slice, create/use a LOINC account and retrieve the documented 2.83 release once. Extract only terms relevant to the draft cases after clinical owner review. Retain the release identifier, source archive hash, required notice, and any applicable EXTERNAL_COPYRIGHT_NOTICE. Do not treat LOINC community mappings as redistributable; the license prohibits copying or distributing that feature's mapping data.
limitations: LOINC 2.83 is the version observed during this research; verify the current release before acquisition.
The complete release is account-authenticated, so the direct download URL is documented but not independently fetched here.
LOINC is a terminology source, not evidence that either New Brunswick hospital uses a particular local test code or workflow.
Third-party embedded content and mapping artifacts may have separate restrictions; inspect the downloaded release's notices before reuse.

sources.title: CMS Healthcare Provider Taxonomy Crosswalk information
sources.period: Published twice yearly, January and July; specific dataset snapshot not verified
sources.grain: Provider/supplier eligibility classification × Healthcare Provider Taxonomy code
useful_fields: dataset release date or version (to capture during acquisition)
observed_facts: CMS describes a data.cms.gov crosswalk linking provider and supplier types eligible for Medicare enrollment with Healthcare Provider Taxonomy codes.
CMS states taxonomy codes are 10-character identifiers and the code set is released twice yearly, in January and July.
The inspected page links to the complete dataset but does not establish a CCN-to-NPI mapping.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Follow CMS's dataset link, identify and record the exact dataset title, downloadable resource URL, release date, and field schema; then retrieve only the current crosswalk snapshot needed to interpret NPPES taxonomy values. Keep taxonomy classification distinct from facility CCN and NPI identity.
limitations: A direct download URL, exact dataset grain/schema, and reuse license were not verified in the inspected page.
Taxonomy classifies provider types; it is not an identifier crosswalk between NPI and CCN.
The source is national and does not validate New Brunswick facility affiliations.

sources.title: NPPES NPI Files
sources.period: Monthly and weekly snapshots; page displayed September 2026 data files during research
sources.grain: NPI provider record, plus separate other-name, practice-location, and endpoint reference files
observed_facts: CMS's NPPES download page lists monthly and weekly downloadable files and describes three included reference files: other names, practice locations, and endpoints.
The page recommends Version 2; it states Version 1 will no longer be supported beginning 2026-03-03.
CMS notes that issuance of an NPI does not ensure that a provider is licensed or credentialed.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For a bounded facility-focused check, download the current NPPES V2 monthly file and its included reference files, filter for the two named hospitals and their known NPIs/names, and preserve the snapshot date and source record identifiers. Use it to inspect NPI identity and reported taxonomy/location only; do not infer CCN equivalence from name similarity.
limitations: The download is a large national file and should be filtered locally after retrieval; this research did not acquire it.
No explicit data reuse license was verified on the inspected page.
NPPES is not a hospital CCN–NPI crosswalk and can include reporting, completeness, and update limitations.

missing_inputs: A specific, independently inspected public CCN–NPI crosswalk with documented release, fields, access, and rights for RWJUH CCN 310038 and Saint Peter's CCN 310070 was not established.
The two draft cases and their intended laboratory observations were not supplied here, so no exact/approximate LOINC matches or bounded code list can be identified.
No source for a local Middlesex County FIPS crosswalk was opened; county FIPS should be sourced and versioned separately from clinical terminology and facility identifiers.
simulation_use: Use LOINC release 2.83 as a candidate, versioned lab-observation vocabulary for a small case-driven term selection after checking the draft cases. Preserve each mapping as an assertion containing source local concept, target code system/code, exact versus approximate status, method, confidence, valid dates, terminology version, and evidence. Keep CCN, NPI, taxonomy, and county FIPS as distinct identifier namespaces; do not infer an equivalence or local facility link without an authoritative crosswalk record.
limitations: Candidate research only; no data were downloaded or incorporated.
Observed web pages and release details require independent verification before acquisition or use.
The public-source findings are not hospital-specific operational data, local estimates, or evidence of local coding practices.
